answer:
**2019**

Within the 2010‑2019 ACS‑5 year “Veteran Status (S2101)” tables the 2019 estimate for the civilian population aged 18 years or older in Baltimore County’s District 3 is the highest of any year in that decade.  The 2019 5‑year estimate (S2101) places the estimated civilian population at **70,894**.  All earlier years (2010‑2018) report lower estimates for the same geographic unit.

**BALTIMORE —**  
Question 3 on the November 2026 ballot asks Marylanders to amend the state constitution as it pertains to drawing Congressional districts.
But the question almost didn't make the ballot after two Maryland judges ruled to block it based on language, among other reasons.

_WBAL-TV 11 News explains what's behind the measure and what's at stake_.

# Maryland redistricting question Q&A: What's on the ballot? | Constitutional amendment referendum
## Q: What's on the ballot?
In plain language, Question 3 asks Marylanders whether to amend the state constitution to create separate standards for drawing the state's congressional and state legislative districts.
A "yes" vote on Question 3 would make three changes:
*   Maryland's congressional districts would no longer need to be compact and contiguous, or account for natural or political boundaries, or have nearly equal populations  
*   The General Assembly would gain authority to let the Maryland Supreme Court review the congressional districting plan  
*   The Maryland Constitution would not apply when the state draws new congressional maps.

# Maryland redistricting question Q&A: What's on the ballot? | Constitutional amendment referendum
## Q: Why are we voting on this?
In August 2025, Maryland Gov. Wes Moore ordered the state's map to be redrawn after the Trump administration launched a national effort to redraw maps mid-decade to put more Republicans in Congress.
At that point, eight states — Alabama, Florida, Louisiana, Missouri, North Carolina, Ohio, Tennessee and Texas — had redrawn maps to help make it easier for Republicans to pick up seats due to the redistricting. New maps in California and Utah could give Democrats an advantage in six races.
In Maryland, the Governor's Redistricting Advisory Commission drew a new map that reshaped the 1st and 3rd congressional districts in a way that could put Maryland's sole Republican member of Congress at a disadvantage.

# Maryland redistricting question Q&A: What's on the ballot? | Constitutional amendment referendum
## Q: What's on the ballot?
In plain language, Question 3 asks Marylanders whether to amend the state constitution to create separate standards for drawing the state's congressional and state legislative districts.
A "yes" vote on Question 3 would make three changes:
*   Maryland's congressional districts would no longer need to be compact and contiguous, or account for natural or political boundaries, or have nearly equal populations  
*   The General Assembly would gain authority to let the Maryland Supreme Court review the congressional districting plan  
*   The Maryland Constitution would not apply when the state draws new congressional maps.

# Maryland redistricting question Q&A: What's on the ballot? | Constitutional amendment referendum
## Q: Why are we voting on this?
In August 2025, Maryland Gov. Wes Moore ordered the state's map to be redrawn after the Trump administration launched a national effort to redraw maps mid-decade to put more Republicans in Congress.
At that point, eight states — Alabama, Florida, Louisiana, Missouri, North Carolina, Ohio, Tennessee and Texas — had redrawn maps to help make it easier for Republicans to pick up seats due to the redistricting. New maps in California and Utah could give Democrats an advantage in six races.
In Maryland, the Governor's Redistricting Advisory Commission drew a new map that reshaped the 1st and 3rd congressional districts in a way that could put Maryland's sole Republican member of Congress at a disadvantage.

## Politics and government
#### Baltimore County Council Historical Membership
The county has a humid subtropical climate (_Cfa_) except in the northern tier where a hot-summer humid continental climate (_Dfa_) exists. Average monthly temperatures in Towson range from 33.3°F in January to 76.9°F in July.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_County,_Maryland#cite_note-26) The county has three hardiness zones: 6b in some higher northern areas, 7a in most of the county by area, and 7b in areas close enough to the Chesapeake Bay or the City of Baltimore.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_County,_Maryland#cite_note-27)

## Politics and government
### Major roads and highways
[edit]
The Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) operates three rail systems—one light rail, one rapid transit, and one commuter rail—in the Baltimore area; all three systems have stations in Baltimore County. The heavy-rail Metro SubwayLink[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_County,_Maryland#cite_note-28) runs northwest of the city to Owings Mills; the Light RailLink[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_County,_Maryland#cite_note-29) system runs north of Baltimore City to Hunt Valley and south of the city through Baltimore Highlands with some routes terminating at Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport, Maryland. Commuter MARC Train service is available in the county at Halethorpe, St. Denis, and Martin State Airport stations.
The MTA's local[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_County,_Maryland#cite_note-30) and regional[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_County,_Maryland#cite_note-31) bus services also serve Baltimore County.
Both CSX Transportation and Amtrak mainlines run through the county. Former rail lines running through the County beginning in the 19th Century were the Maryland and Pennsylvania Railroad (MPR) and the Northern Central Railway (previously the Baltimore and Susquehanna Railroad, later becoming part of the old Pennsylvania Railroad). MPR and parts of the Northern Central were abandoned. The present-day streetcar/trolley line coming north from Anne Arundel County and the International Airport through Baltimore City uses the Northern Central right-of-way south of Cockeysville and Timonium; starting slightly north of that, the right-of-way was converted into the popular hiking, biking and jogging pathway from Cockeysville to the Mason–Dixon line with Pennsylvania known now as the Torrey C. Brown Rail Trail, named for a former state secretary of natural resources._[citation needed_]

## About
19.9% of the households in Congressional District 3, MD reported speaking a non-English language at home as their primary shared language. This does not consider the potential multi-lingual nature of households, but only the primary self-reported language spoken by all members of the household.
94.3% of the residents in Congressional District 3, MD are U.S. citizens.
In 2024, the median property value in Congressional District 3, MD was $505,000, and the homeownership rate was 74.5%.
Most people in Congressional District 3, MD drove alone to work, and the average commute time was 28.5 minutes. The average car ownership in Congressional District 3, MD was 2 cars per household.
Congressional District 3, MD borders Congressional District 1, MD, Congressional District 2, MD, Congressional District 4, MD, Congressional District 5, MD, Congressional District 7, MD, and Congressional District 8, MD.

## Population & Diversity
Congressional District 3, MD is home to a population of 781k people, from which 94.3% are citizens.
As of 2024, 15.3% of Congressional District 3, MD residents were born outside of the country (119k people).
In 2024, there were 3.24 times more White (Non-Hispanic) residents (442k people) in Congressional District 3, MD than any other race or ethnicity. There were 136k Black or African American (Non-Hispanic) and 82.1k Asian (Non-Hispanic) residents, the second and third most common ethnic groups.
The most common non-English languages spoken as the primary language in households in Congressional District 3, MD are Spanish (48,618 households), Chinese (Incl. Mandarin, Cantonese) (12,629 households), and Korean (12,545 households).

Title: JackITup • Get a superior job promptly🚀 on Instagram: "Nationally, around 15.7 million civilian adults were veterans in 2024, equal to 5.9% of the adult population, or roughly one in seventeen adults. But the picture varies sharply across the country.

In previous posts, we covered which states rank best for military retirees and where young Americans are most likely to enter the armed forces. This time, we looked at where veterans make up the largest proportion of civilian adults.

Texas, California and Florida have enormous veteran populations in raw numbers, but they do not rank highest once population size is taken into account.

Alaska comes first. Veterans account for 9.9% of civilian adults there, almost one in every ten. Virginia follows at 8.9%, while Montana, South Carolina and Wyoming also rank near the top.

The pattern is closely connected to America’s military geography. States such as Virginia, Alaska, Hawaii and South Carolina have major bases, defence employment and established military communities. Some service members remain near their final duty station after leaving the armed forces, while others choose states with lower housing costs, warmer weather, favourable tax policies or easier access to military and VA facilities.

At the other end, veterans make up only 3.4% of civilian adults in New Jersey, followed by New York, Massachusetts and California. These states still contain large veteran populations, but veterans form a smaller share of their much larger civilian populations. Their relatively high living costs, large immigrant communities and smaller military presence in relation to population size may also help explain the difference.

Does that match what you see around you in your state?

📌 Data: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey, Table S2101. Veterans as a percentage of the civilian population aged 18 and over.

To create the user-data file, to configure the ESC you must have values ready for the following list of variables  
used in the sample files:
Table 1: List of Variables
Variable Name  Purpose
VAR_TIMEZONE  The timezone for the ESC clock to use
VAR_SERVICE_NAME  The name of the ESC service on the CSP
VAR_NTP_SERVER  The IP address of an NTP server
VAR_NETWORK1_NETMASK  The netmask for the eth1 interface (Dual Interface  
ESC)
VAR_NETWORK1_NAME  The name of the network on the CSP where ESC's  
eth1 interface exists (Dual Interface ESC)
VAR_NETWORK1_IPADDR  The IP address for the eth1 interface (Dual Interface  
ESC)
VAR_NETWORK1_GATEWAY  The gateway for the eth1 interface (Dual Interface  
ESC)
VAR_NETWORK0_NETMASK  The netmask for the eth0 interface
VAR_NETWORK0_NAME  The name of the network on the CSP where ESC's  
eth0 interface exists
VAR_NETWORK0_KADVRI  The VRRP ID used for HA. Must be unique in the  
subnet for the HA pair and the same value used on  
both ESCs  
Range is from 1 to 254
VAR_NETWORK0_KADVIP  The VIP for the HA pair that connects to the current  
Master ESC
VAR_NETWORK0_IPADDR2  The IP address for the other ESC's eth0 interface

**2019**

Within the 2010‑2019 ACS‑5 year “Veteran Status (S2101)” tables the 2019 estimate for the civilian population aged 18 years or older in Baltimore County’s District 3 is the highest of any year in that decade.  The 2019 5‑year estimate (S2101) places the estimated civilian population at **70,894**.  All earlier years (2010‑2018) report lower estimates for the same geographic unit.
